mistakes.note: The sabotage reveal does not hold together: Vane's skin was cut in his border post's stores two evenings before the caravan reached it (M76), Jory then confesses to cutting one for the keeper 'at the Well', and everyone treats it as the same deed; the Journal, what Tamsin and Vane know, the summary and a round 38 Choice all say Jory cut it at the border post, which the page never showed and Vane's own dating rules out.
Jory says 'She's right' about the fifth rider closing a gate, which Wren only thought and never said aloud.
The satchel that rode against Wren's ribs (M2) and under her forearm (M16) is suddenly lashed to the camel's saddle, so it bolts away with the camel.
Ossery says four grey riders passed his well at dusk and the narration takes it as true, but at dusk those four were striking the caravan hours down the road.
Tamsin throws back at Ossery what he 'told me last night' about not having the pay to be curious; he said it to Wren and Vane hours before her caravan arrived.
Vane puts his border post two hundred leagues from the Well, when the caravan covered the distance in a day and a half.

Vane, ordered to see the cargo safe to Kesh and having said everyone rides the Flats together (M72, M74), is left behind at the Well without a word or a decision on the page as the riders who shot Wren arrive.
Wren rides 'her camel' with her waterskin, though her camel was left in the hollow with only the satchel taken (M46) and was never shown coming back.
The Journal adds the crossbow woman as a Known NPC named Sefa, with a portrait under that name; nobody on the page has named her.
Story time reads day 3, 7th of Dry Month, small hours of the 8th of Dry Month: the date is a day behind, and the time of day carries its own date from then on.
A Choice offers to pick out 'the crossbow man'; the page made the crossbow rider a woman at M4.
A Choice tells Tamsin the yard holds 'only Ossery behind his barred door', after Ossery came out with his tin box and ledger at first light (M64).

Loose Ends still open at the end though the page answered them: whether Wren can recover her camel and rejoin the caravan (M46, M66), and who the rider raising the eastern dust is (it became the storm wall at M84).

Journal left stale: Tamsin's summary never moves past 'associated with the caravan and checks the camel line', Vane's still has him riding with the caravan after he stays at the Well, and the fact that the eastern dust may be the fifth rider stays after it is a storm.
What Tamsin and Vane know is recorded twice in near-identical entries (again in rounds 12 and 14) until a later summary folds them.
An invented cut scar runs down his forehead, and the neck burn is drawn as a thin cut.
Jory's hair is dark brown, not red, here and again in the M66 picture.
Wren sits upright and smiling behind Vane with no bolt or binding, at a moment she is slumped with a bolt through her shoulder.
Wren rides in front of Vane, who carries the satchel, on a grey horse; the page has her behind him with the satchel on her back, and the horse was bay in the M2 and M46 pictures.
The wound is shown raw and unbound on her right shoulder, in a sleeveless top; the page has the left shoulder, bound shoulder to chest.
Ossery wears a khaki army greatcoat, and in the M66 picture is a dark man in a fez; his portrait and the page give him an old blue Border Guard coat.
Tamsin kneels in the sand and Vane is nowhere, at the moment he walks up and confronts her standing.
The crossbow woman walks on foot among the caravan's drivers rather than riding down the far crest with two others, and her prompt gives her the PC's reference picture and short black hair.

choices.reason: Three real paths most rounds and the picks bend the story (running for the Well, standing by Vane, taking the fall), but a watch-the-dust option recurs through rounds 8 to 12 and two wordings are stale.

surprise.reason: The fifth rider's flanking, the lone shape over the hollow, the riders walking into the Well as travellers and Vane turning on Tamsin all land from what was set up out of sight; the dusk strike is signposted and the Free Wells never reach the page.

threads.reason: The riders' thread moves with story time and bends to every pick, the sabotage thread reaches the Well on its day and the storm is woven in, but the sabotage thread is muddied by an invented border-post skin and patron.

characters.reason: Vane and Tamsin have voices and wants of their own, but Tamsin quotes a talk she never heard, Vane drops his own word and orders without a line, and Jory answers a thought.

continuity.reason: The wound, the lost knife, the route and the clock hold for 35 rounds, then the waterskin reveal contradicts itself, on top of the satchel's move to the saddle, the riders at the Well at dusk and the returning camel.

pacing.reason: Every reply adds a fact, a turn or a decision, the night ride keeps its tension over seven replies and the hours on the road are skipped only when the pick asked.

prose.reason: Vivid, dry and in one voice with lines worth keeping, held back by a few garbled lines (M19, M27, M46) and tics such as unhurried, honest and doing sums.

pictures.reason: People and places are recognisable, but more than half the scene pictures carry a wrong detail: the wound on the wrong shoulder or missing, Jory's hair, Ossery's coat, the horse, Tamsin kneeling without Vane.

secrets.reason: The letter's content, Tamsin's saddle and the Free Wells stay hidden and the sabotage comes out through Jory on the page; the only leak is Sefa's name in the Journal.

agency.reason: Wren's moves are carried out in indirect speech as given, and both Continues leave her deciding nothing; a gesture to Jory and a read of Ossery go slightly past the move.

stakes.reason: Nine Checks on the risky moves, and failures cost: the bolt through the shoulder and the lost knife last the whole run, the pistol stays refused, Ossery clams up; the rolled fall is won but loses the camel.

state.reason: Inventory, status, lore and the bench's actions are kept true, but the Journal states a deed the page never showed, names Sefa, keeps stale summaries and Loose Ends, and story time carried a wrong date for a round.

adventure.reason: Each stage is its own place with its own danger, from the standoff in the spires through the dusk strike, the moonlit chase after the camel and the pinch to the well and the white flats under a storm wall, and the player's picks decide how she comes through, at a lasting cost.

violence.reason: The bolt strike, the fall and the drawing of the shaft are clear and physical and the pain is carried through every later scene, but each blow is over in a line or two.
